nodes.label: Adjunction never repairs a closed index
nodes.rationale: One-line proof on the graph S' = {(x, h(x))}: the join of (x,h(x)) and (y,h(y)) is (x v y, h(x) v h(y)), so S' closed forces S closed, and meets likewise. The contrapositive is the working statement — a non-closed set stays non-closed under the adjunction of any function of its own coordinates.

nodes.label: Lambda x h is closed exactly when h is a lattice homomorphism
nodes.rationale: Measured at 100 per cent over 424 tests: projections, minima and constants qualify; sums, products and differences do not. A difference fails because over x v y the two terms take their maxima independently, so e - l of the join need not equal the larger difference, and the graph breaks.

nodes.label: Only three routes to repair remain: enlarge, restrict, reorder
nodes.rationale: The theorem is what leaves exactly three repairs — add cells, remove cells, or reorder and change neither. Adjoining a derived axis is none of these and is ruled out at the source.

hyperedges.label: A derived coordinate cannot repair closure
